check: Complete the onboarding flow from start through New York terminal/survivor/extraction
pass_signal: Player can proceed without external instructions.

check: Exercise every control in control_remap_manifest.tsv
pass_signal: Every input fires once and no modal UI leakage occurs.

check: Cycle Story, Easy, Normal, Hard, Survival, Nightmare from pause menu
pass_signal: Label updates, save persists, new spawns use expected multipliers.

check: Toggle subtitles, subtitle size, high contrast, color vision, reduced motion, simplified hints, aim assist, reset defaults, and control profile export
pass_signal: Each setting has an observable runtime effect, readouts preview queued changes before Apply, reset does not overwrite audio mix, and export writes a reviewable control profile.

check: Save, quit, relaunch, load, continue after terminal/survivor/zombie progress, and inspect death/victory language-run summaries
pass_signal: State restores without duplicate objectives or resource loss, and end-state screens identify the start-screen language resume slot.

check: Start new Java, C, C+, C++, Python, and MATLAB runs; resume at least two saved languages; submit one failed and one passing terminal attempt
pass_signal: Start screen always appears, each language has NEW and RESUME actions, terminals stay locked to the chosen track, validation output shows Language Run Lock, and attempts/solves update only that language save profile.

check: Launch the game cold and after at least two language saves exist; inspect the start screen before choosing New or Resume
pass_signal: FIRST-SESSION ROUTE PREVIEW and LANGUAGE SAVE ROSTER appear before gameplay, explain protected terminal -> survivor marker -> extraction, name the language-only save slot/resume state, show Java, C, C+, C++, Python, and MATLAB as RESUME AVAILABLE or NEW RUN READY, and all New/Resume rows remain selectable.

check: Start a selected-language terminal, enter a correct solution, press PRACTICE RUN [Ctrl+P], close/reopen the terminal, then press VALIDATE CODE; repeat with an incorrect solution
pass_signal: Practice output shows PRACTICE RUN - NO SAVE ADVANCE, PRACTICE-ONLY DEBRIEF, Practice Run Lock, unchanged save profile, no survivor route unlock, no ResearchPoints/coding score/attempt/streak/survivor intel archive update, and live validation remains available.

check: Live-solve a selected-language terminal, claim each reward option on separate fresh runs, close/reopen before claim, save/quit/resume before claim, then claim and attempt a second claim
pass_signal: Reward choice is unavailable after practice/bypass, available after live solve, persists through start-screen Resume until claimed, grants exactly one Research Boost, Field Kit, or Crafting Cache, disables after claim, and cannot be duplicated by reopening the terminal.

check: Solve or bypass a terminal in one selected-language run, close the terminal, open J, save/quit, relaunch from the start-screen Resume action, and open J again
pass_signal: LAST LEARNING DEBRIEF names the same language, save slot, challenge, concept, score, and saved post-solve or assisted learning takeaway before and after resume.

check: Solve or bypass a terminal in one selected-language run, open J, save/quit, relaunch from the start-screen Resume action for that language, open J again, rescue the matching survivor, save/relaunch again
pass_signal: SURVIVOR INTEL ARCHIVE names the same selected language, save slot, terminal, contact, route, score, and clean/assisted upload summary after resume, then updates to RESCUED after the survivor rescue persists.

check: Start a selected-language run, open J before terminal solve, solve the terminal, open J again on the survivor route, rescue the survivor, open J at extraction, save/quit, resume from the start screen, and open J again
pass_signal: FAIL-SAFE OBJECTIVE BOARD names the selected language, save slot, start-screen Resume availability, active route phase, return markers, T objective jump, Backspace/F8 safe recovery, J journal, P/Esc pause/save, protected terminal safety, and next action before and after resume.

check: Start a selected-language run, stand inside the safehouse/terminal lab, lure or spawn a zombie near the entrance, then step outside onto the city route
pass_signal: Inside the tagged learning space zombies do not chase, elite abilities do not fire, boomer/explosion damage is blocked, and zombie pressure resumes only after the player leaves the protected zone.

check: In one selected-language run, inspect the Civilian Support Hub, use Engineer, Medic, Scientist, and Trader services where preconditions allow, save/relaunch, then wait for a day-night flip and repeat one service
pass_signal: HUD prompts name each role benefit, used services remain unavailable after relaunch in that language profile, day-night reset refreshes the service list, and another language profile keeps its own support-service state.

check: In one selected-language run, inspect Engineer, Medic, Scientist, and Trader NPCs, use one available service, retry a used service, try Medic while healthy, and try Trader without five scrap
pass_signal: idle support motion, success acknowledgment, cooldown refusal, precondition refusal, role light pulse, HUD service prompts, and selected-language cooldown persistence remain visible without moving the collision body.

check: Start fresh Java and Python runs, create a save in each, return to the start screen, inspect the start-screen resume row, then resume each language and inspect HUD plus cast-stage ACTIVE OPERATOR PROFILE signage
pass_signal: Each language profile shows the expected saved operator callsign and role, the start-screen resume row names that operator, HUD displays Operator: callsign (role), and gameplay still begins from language selection rather than a separate character picker.

check: Start a selected-language run, approach the survivor before solving the terminal, solve the terminal, rescue the survivor, open the journal, save/relaunch, and inspect the route again
pass_signal: The survivor role marker, HUD prompt, relief-camp profile card, rescue subtitle, dispatch line, companion handoff, journal dossier, and selected-language save state agree on the survivor archetype, icon, field need, and rescue value.

check: Approach a survivor before terminal solve, attempt rescue, solve the selected-language terminal, then rescue the survivor while watching the body and rescue light
pass_signal: idle motion, locked refusal, rescue gesture, light pulse, immediate collision disable, delayed fade-out, and selected-language save updates are visible and do not disturb the start-screen resume flow.

check: Start a selected-language run, step out of the protected coding safehouse into the city route, let a regular/director/horde zombie acquire the player, then step back into the protected learning zone
pass_signal: The threat compass names standard pursuit state, captions call out pursuit/closing/attack windup, attacks wait for the readable telegraph before applying damage, and pressure stops inside protected coding space without breaking selected-language saves.

check: Fight a regular/director/horde zombie outside the safehouse, shoot without killing it, let it attack once, then step back into protected learning space
pass_signal: chase sway, attack windup, lunge, hit recoil, and protected learning hold poses are visible without changing collision, save behavior, or coding-zone safety.

check: Fight a promoted skeletal zombie outside the safehouse, land nonfatal body/head/limb hits, then kill it and repeat against an unpromoted fallback zombie
pass_signal: Promoted zombies briefly blend through PhysicalAnimationComponent hit flinches, fallback zombies still show launch/glow/pose feedback, living mesh collision resets, and death ragdoll or primitive corpse physics remains authoritative.

check: Inspect New York entry, arena, safehouse, armory, terminal, survivor, helipad, character stage, and Mac hair-card/groom review intake
pass_signal: City identity reads clearly, route remains passable, and strand groom sources are not presented as packaged Mac runtime hair.

check: Walk from the entry pad through downtown, civic, transit, medical, and survivor-search districts while inspecting roads, sidewalks, crosswalks, facades, shop doors, shop windows, awnings, and store-role labels
pass_signal: The route reads as an actual city street grid with ground-floor storefront shells, crosswalks and curb cues stay nonblocking, and storefront dressing remains a world-promotion target rather than blocking gameplay.

check: Walk entry, armory, safehouse, language marker, terminal, survivor, and helipad critical path while brushing nearby dressing and cover
pass_signal: Route labels are readable, decorative route-adjacent actors remain nonblocking, and every critical access zone is passable without snagging on doors, stairs, cover, or fallback props.

check: Fight default, elite, and boss-adjacent threats after zombie variant promotion validation
pass_signal: Windup, glow, damage direction, stagger, death feedback, promoted zombie meshes, and locomotion AnimBPs are legible.

check: Take repeated zombie hits with full health, armor, low health, medkits, and no medkits
pass_signal: The health label, damage alert, mitigation text, armor use, mercy window, per-hit cap, emergency medkit, critical callout, and death save/quit options are understandable and no healthy player is killed by one ordinary hit.

check: Force death in a selected-language run, use resume, force death again, then use save-and-quit and relaunch through the start screen
pass_signal: Death count persists, resume keeps the same language profile, replay starts from the city entry pad with health above zero, save-and-quit creates a start-screen language resume option, and fresh restart deletes only that language save.

check: Fight a regular city wave, physics ambush, encounter director wave, language breach patrol, dog den, terminal horde, elite mini-boss, boomer add, and boss phase add
pass_signal: Every threat carries a readable family label or tag, city-weighted variants stay consistent after save/load, and transient horde/add spawns remain readable without bloating save data.

check: Load the survivor approach before terminal solve, after terminal solve, and from a low-health or low-ammo save
pass_signal: The DIRECTOR STATE board names objective/resource state, route-locked pressure feels lighter, route-open pressure feels urgent, relief pickups appear only for low-resource resumes, and role markers remain readable.

check: In one selected-language run, interact with a terminal, survivor, friendly NPC, pickup, case file, helipad, and Jeep; then fight zombies near barricades
pass_signal: E prompts resolve only usable objects, weapon fire still hits zombies and cover, zombie sight respects cover, pickups/case files collect, and the selected-language save flow is unchanged.

check: Throw flares and smoke at physics targets, kill zombies, break barricades, drive the Jeep fallback over marked surfaces, and inspect stress-rig props
pass_signal: Throwable arcs, impact nudges, ragdoll/fallback corpse motion, debris retirement, Jeep surface cues, and loose props stay readable across frame-rate swings while actors/components carry fixed-step review tags.

check: Fight through the physics ambush and encounter director cover using shots, melee, throwables, and zombie pressure
pass_signal: Wood barricades visibly crack, break into short-lived debris, zombies attack blocking cover, and the player can use cover without active debris or fallback props trapping the route.

check: Inspect player, first-person arms, survivor, friendly NPC, companion, zombie, and boss skeletal actors after runtime spawn
pass_signal: Every live skeletal path carries IK/Control Rig slot tags, keeps its fallback animation readable, and has a documented promotion target for authored IK Rig, IK Retargeter, Control Rig, and Maya cleanup work.

check: Inspect the DCC FOOT IK station and runtime tags on player, survivor, friendly NPC, companion, zombie, and boss skeletal actors
pass_signal: Every full-body skeletal path carries FootGroundingRuntimeContract, FootIKGroundingReview, ControlRigFootContactReady, FootPlantTraceReady, and PelvisOffsetReview tags, while first-person arms carry FootGroundingExcluded_FirstPersonArms.

check: Walk the DCC cleanup bay and inspect bind pose, skeleton names, sockets, animation takes, LOD/material, physics asset, FBX export, and promotion stations; then inspect live skeletal actors for cleanup tags
pass_signal: Every promoted character path has clear Maya cleanup evidence before replacing fallback meshes, sockets, AnimBPs, physics assets, or montage-ready clips.

check: Solve a city terminal, approach the warden runway, then fight charger, spitter, and boomer mini-boss sentinels
pass_signal: The runway changes from dormant to active after terminal intel, each mini-boss role is readable, neutralized sentinels persist across reload, and the boss reveal/phase telegraphs remain intact.

check: Use Mira/Tomas/Ada/Noor/Briggs as medic, engineer, rifle support, scout, and heavy rescue around combat
pass_signal: Named role labels, barks, pips, order responses, and tactical behaviors feel distinct.

check: Use Y/U/O/N with the rescue squad, let a companion fire at a nearby zombie, trigger medic support, and take companion damage in a selected-language run
pass_signal: role signal light, idle follow/hold pose, support-fire recoil, medic pulse, order acknowledgment, and damage flinch are visible without companion capsules blocking the player or altering the language save.

check: Submit practice, correct, and incorrect answers across lesson families
pass_signal: Feedback names failed checks, points to a next repair step, practice runs state no save advance, successful live solves show concept proof, language transfer, save continuity, and survivor-route follow-up plus reward choice kiosk availability, the journal survivor dossier updates after terminal solve and rescue, and the survivor rescue subtitle names route, language, helipad, save, and dossier state.

check: Start a fresh city and inspect the queued radio briefing before and after HUD startup; then test terminal locked, survivor route open, and extraction beacon live states
pass_signal: Radio Relay subtitle names language, terminal, survivor, landmark, current phase, and next step while respecting subtitle toggle/scale/high-contrast settings.

check: Approach calm street, one zombie, close pursuit, critical range, and protected safehouse boundary
pass_signal: Music intensity summary/captions shift calm/watch/pursuit/critical and damp inside protected learning space while SFX/music volume settings remain respected.

check: Walk entry, protected coding lab, safehouse exterior, street grid, survivor route, survivor camp, and extraction pad before and after terminal/rescue progress
pass_signal: [Ambient] captions and audio summaries name the active zone and future bed key while selected-language save/resume behavior remains unchanged.

check: Toggle Visualize Sound Cues in Settings, then walk calm street, close pursuit, protected coding lab, survivor route, and extraction pad with subtitles on and off
pass_signal: HUD SOUND CUES line appears only when enabled and names threat intensity, ambient zone, and caption state without disturbing selected-language save/resume behavior.

check: Toggle Mono Audio in Settings, confirm Visualize Sound Cues stays enabled, fire/dry-fire/hit targets, approach zombie attacks/growls, rescue a survivor, and pass through active ambient city zones
pass_signal: Audio mix summary shows Mono on, project-owned positional cues remain centered/playable, active ambient and growl components refresh without restart, and selected-language saves restore the mono setting.

check: Set Subtitle Size to 0.75x and UI Text Size to 1.75x, apply, save, restart/resume a language run, then invert the two values and inspect subtitles, HUD, terminal, journal, minimap, save slots, fast travel, pause, tutorial, damage feedback, victory, and death screens
pass_signal: UI surfaces follow UI Text Size, active captions follow Subtitle Size, both values persist independently, and reset defaults returns both to 1.0x without changing audio mix.

check: Collect terminal evidence, survivor note, and route brief in one city
pass_signal: Each case file shows a CASE FILE subtitle, the journal case-file summary updates, and relaunch keeps collected files hidden in the selected-language run.

check: Walk the environmental story deck before and after a terminal solve, inspect automation failure, safehouse engineer network, survivor stake, code cause/effect, and city chapter cards
pass_signal: The story deck is readable and nonblocking, explains why coding rescues people, and does not alter selected-language save, protected safehouse, combat, terminal, or extraction behavior.

check: Walk the field world-bible deck and inspect premise, pillars, factions/forces, technology rules, and per-city lore cards
pass_signal: The lore deck is readable and nonblocking, keeps the canonical premise coherent, and does not alter selected-language save, protected safehouse, combat, terminal, or extraction behavior.

check: Inspect objective beacon before terminal solve, after solve, after rescue, and with Reduced Motion enabled
pass_signal: RADIO SCAN, SURVIVOR PING, and RESCUE BEACON labels update in-world, the extraction halo appears after rescue, and reduced motion still shows text-first phase changes.

check: Inspect several city indices at the helipad and open the fast-travel menu after rescue
pass_signal: Rooftop, convoy, boat, rail, bridge, or helipad-command staging is visible, labeled, nonblocking, and does not interfere with the fast-travel menu.

check: Walk the cinematic street route and inspect intro, language, terminal, survivor, extraction, and boss reveal camera markers
pass_signal: Each beat has a visible camera rail/tripod/lens or fallback reveal marker, remains nonblocking, respects reduced-motion fallback intent, and gives future Sequencer/Control Rig assets a clear replacement target.

check: Collect scanner, flashlight, ammo pouch, bypass kit, medkit, and armor pickups; use L flashlight, Z scanner, and Ctrl+B bypass kit inside a terminal in the selected language run
pass_signal: HUD counts update, pickups autosave into the selected language save slot, the flashlight emits light, scanner spends a charge, and terminal bypass opens the survivor route while preserving the selected language.

check: Inspect the tactical armory, press each 1-0 quick slots key, fire or reload at least two weapons, save, relaunch, and resume the same selected-language profile
pass_signal: HUD QUICK SLOTS row matches the armory board, active weapon marker updates for every key, and active slot plus magazine/reserve values persist after save/resume.

check: Cycle all weapon slots in first-person, fire ammo weapons, reload partial magazines, and trigger the no-ammo melee fallback
pass_signal: Each weapon family shows a distinct stance, silhouette, recoil, reload, and melee fallback while the HUD text remains readable.

check: Fire multiple weapon families; confirm a body hit, headshot, barricade hit, area hit, reload, dry fire, melee fallback, and incoming damage
pass_signal: Camera/weapon feedback should show body hit, headshot, barricade hit, area hit, reload, dry fire, melee fallback, and incoming damage without disrupting HUD readability or reduced-motion comfort.

check: Walk to hospital, school, store, transit, and civic records rooms; enter each open-front room and collect its functional pickup
pass_signal: Player can enter each room without snagging on the doorway, read the mission board, and see the pickup affect the selected-language run.

check: Walk through the entry weather shelter, safehouse light pool, and rescue route sky cue in at least two city climate families
pass_signal: Text-first climate labels, ground reflections, weather streaks, and signal lights are visible, nonblocking, and distinct from objective markers.

check: Walk through the regional kit entry gate, landmark vista kit, and objective district kit in at least three city art-kit families
pass_signal: Kit bible labels, landmark vista, modular swatches, regional motif, and signal lights are visible, nonblocking, and tied to the city art kit, region, district, and landmark.

check: Walk near zombies quietly with cover, then sprint, fire, use scanner, toggle flashlight, throw utility gear, and enter a protected coding space
pass_signal: HUD moves between QUIET, LOW NOISE, AUDIBLE, NOISY, and EXPOSED; zombies investigate noise or chase sightlines; protected coding space still suppresses detection and selected-language saves remain unchanged.

pass_signal: Runtime Data Layer station is readable and nonblocking, actor tags cover safehouse/combat/weather/objective states, and solving a terminal opens route cues without changing selected-language save/resume behavior.

pass_signal: Player can read each concept room, match the selected lesson to the artifact, inspect all eight validator archetypes with visible test, hidden test, mistake marker, mentor proxy, and survivor proxy, and return to the safe terminal without combat or traversal interference.
